title: Cross-layer memory governor for hotspot isolation and dynamic headroom budgeting
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We frequently see transient OOMs and tail-latency spikes when multi-tenant continuous-batching workloads overlap high-KV-pressure traces with large weight residency requirements (long-context models). Current static reservations (weights vs activations vs KV) are either too conservative (wasting GPU capacity) or too brittle (leading to eviction storms and OOMs).

Goal: Implement a cross-layer memory governor that continuously budgets and rebalances memory across weights, KV cache, and activations at runtime. The governor should isolate 'hotspot' tenants/requests, create temporary micro-reserves (headroom) for predicted bursts, and gracefully degrade KV fidelity (eviction/compression) when necessary to protect SLOs. The solution must be observable, feature-flag controllable, and default to safe fallbacks if telemetry is unavailable.

Design principles: 1) Predictive but conservative: use short-horizon forecasting of KV pressure + activation growth to provision micro-headroom without starving long-lived weight residency. 2) Cross-layer arbitration: budget shifts are decided by a single governor component that has visibility of weights residency, live KV occupancy, and active activation footprints coming from the batching scheduler. 3) Non-disruptive fallback: provide immediate hard-fail-safe behavior (strict watermarks) if governor fails. 4) Tenant-aware priorities: support per-tenant soft-wallets so critical customers can retain higher headroom.

What this ticket delivers: a first production-ready implementation of the governor focused on the following capabilities:
- Live memory accounting collector: unified per-GPU view of weights, KV, activations, ephemeral allocations.
- Micro-reserve allocator: ephemeral headroom slots that can be granted to the batching scheduler for short-lived spikes (with TTL and refund semantics).
- Priority lanes and eviction policy: ordered eviction lanes (LRU, compression-first) for KV with throttles to avoid eviction storms.
- Governor decision loop: periodic (configurable) reconcile loop implementing heuristics + simple predictive model using moving windows of KV occupancy and activation growth rate.
- Telemetry + gating: metrics exported to Console and rollout gated by feature flag (mem_governor_v1).

This ticket intentionally avoids complex ML forecasting for v1; we'll use deterministic heuristics and simple exponential smoothing. Future tickets will iterate on the predictive model and per-model kernels.
acceptance_criteria: Unified per-GPU memory accounting available in telemetry (weights, kv_size_bytes, activations_estimate_bytes, ephemeral_reserved_bytes)
Governor can allocate ephemeral headroom and return refunds when not consumed; no headroom leaks across requests after 30s TTL
Under guided stressbench (see test plan), p95 token latency increase <= 10% compared to baseline and OOM incidence is reduced by >= 95% during 3x burst scenarios
Canary rollout (5% traffic) completes without increasing error rate or exceeding SLOs for 72 hours
Feature is behind mem_governor_v1 flag and system falls back to strict watermarks when flag disabled or governor crashes
implementation_plan: Phase 0 - Simulation (2w): add synthetic workload generator to memory-sim harness to validate heuristics and tune TTLs for micro-reserves
Phase 1 - Collector + Telemetry (1w): implement unified memory accounting in runtime and expose metrics + debug endpoint
Phase 2 - Micro-reserve allocator (2w): implement ephemeral headroom allocator API used by batching scheduler; include refund API and TTL enforcement
Phase 3 - Eviction lanes (2w): implement ordered KV eviction lanes with compression-first policy and soft-throttles to prevent eviction storms
Phase 4 - Governor loop + safety (1w): implement reconcile loop and fail-safe strict watermarks; wire up feature flag and config knobs
Phase 5 - Canary + observability (1w): deploy to canary pool, enable detailed dashboards and alerts (OOM spike, eviction rate, headroom churn), iterate on knobs
Phase 6 - Gradual rollout (2w): ramp canary to 25% -> 60% -> 100% with automated rollback criteria defined in rollout_steps
risks_mitigation: Risk: Governor misallocates and starves weight residency causing degraded model throughput. Mitigation: hard floor for weights residency; any governor step must maintain weights_reserved >= 90% of baseline or abort change.
Risk: Eviction storm causes high downstream latencies. Mitigation: implement soft-throttles and slow ramp of eviction rate; add exponential backoff if downstream latency increases.
Risk: Telemetry gaps lead to unsafe decisions. Mitigation: governor defaults to strict watermarks when telemetry stale > 10s and emits alert for operator action.
Risk: Complexity increases debugging time. Mitigation: debug endpoints that can dump per-GPU decision trace and recent reconciles; log level toggles in runtime.
test_plan: Unit tests for memory accounting collector and micro-reserve lifecycle (create, consume, refund, TTL expiry)
Integration tests with continuous-batching scheduler to validate request path for ephemeral grants and refunds
Stressbench: 1000 mixed-tenancy traces with 2x-3x KV bursts to validate p95 tail and OOM reduction targets
Chaos test: inject delayed telemetry and confirm governor falls back to strict watermarks without OOMs
Canary validation: 72h canary with automatic rollback on increase in OOM_count or p95 latency > baseline + 10%
rollout_steps: Feature flag implementation behind mem_governor_v1; default off in prod
Deploy to internal staging and run the stressbench; collect baseline metrics and tune TTLs
Enable feature for 5% of production traffic on isolated canary GPUs for 72h with extended logging
If canary metrics pass, ramp to 25% for 48h, then 60% for 24h while monitoring key metrics; allow manual rollback at each gate
Full rollout to 100% only after 7 days of stable metrics and no critical incidents
Post-rollout: schedule a post-mortem analysis and knob sweeps (eviction throttle, TTLs, headroom size)
